goalReviews.assessableSingleCompetence: Explain the link between independently orienting/segregating different homologous pairs and different combinations of whole parental-origin chromosomes in given gamete models.
goalReviews.textFindings: Different homologous pairs are explicit in DE and EN. Neither segment exchange nor an additional probability routine is requested. No compulsory text repair identified.
goalReviews.learnerMustExplain: The choice of a maternal/paternal partner in one pair does not force the choice in another pair, and the shown different gamete combinations follow from these different pair orientations/segregations.
nonEvidence: Reading only the colors or supplied labels
Repeating a full supplied causal conclusion
requiredContextConditions: At least two different homologous pairs
Correctly given alternative orientations and gamete sets
One chromosome of each represented type remains in the output
Do not label all four alternatives as required outcomes of a single pictured meiosis

goalReviews.assessableSingleCompetence: Explain the link between exchange of corresponding non-sister chromatid segments in a homologous pair and recombinant parental-information regions in the given output.
goalReviews.textFindings: Non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes and corresponding segments are now explicit in DE and EN. No compulsory text repair identified.
goalReviews.learnerMustExplain: The corresponding exchanged regions account for a participating chromatid combining parental information differently; regions are retained rather than created or lost.
nonEvidence: Substituting nonhomologous exchange, only sister-chromatid exchange or numerical chromosome errors
requiredContextConditions: Corresponding region positions and meaningful parental origin/information markers
Correct provided gamete sets to which recombinant chromatids can be traced
Do not claim each real exchange necessarily creates a new allele or additional gene

givensVersusEvidence: Correct terms, structures, process views and outcomes may be provided. The complete causal explanation must not already be provided as the assessed answer.
